paper.title: Bandit Learning with Delayed Impact of Actions

unmapped: Action is a meta arm p in the K-simplex; each base arm k is activated independently with probability p_k and its reward observed; expected utility sum_k p_k r_k(p_k) with unknown Lipschitz r_k (impact function f(t)=p(t), gamma=0)
settings.definition_quote: When action $\vp(t)$ is taken at time $t$, the institution obtains an expected reward $\Totalrew_t(\vp(t)) = \sum_{k=1}^K p_k(t) \cdot \rewfn_k \left(f_k(t)\right)$ ... In this section, we study \action, in which the impact function $\bm{\mathrm{f}}(t)=\vp(t)$

unmapped: Mean rewards depend on the action history through a time-discounted average impact f_k(t)=sum_s p_k(s) gamma^{t-s}/sum_s gamma^{t-s}, gamma in (0,1)
Learner knows the discount factor gamma (input to the algorithm)
Meta arm in the simplex with independent activation of base arms; utility sum_k p_k r_k(f_k(t)); regret against best fixed meta arm
settings.definition_quote: we focus on the setting in which $\bm{\mathrm{f}}(t)$ is a time-discounted average, with each component $f_k(t)$ defined as $f_k(t) = \frac{\sum_{s=1}^{t} p_k(s) \gamma^{t-s} }{\sum_{s=1}^{t} \gamma^{t-s}}$

source.label: theorem:key_theorem_vanilla
source.quote: Let $\epsilon=\Theta\big((\ln T/T)^{1/3}\big)$. The regret of Algorithm \ref{algo:action_UCB} (with respect to the optimal arm in non-discretized $\cP$) is upper bounded as follows: $\reg(T) = \cO\big(KT^{2/3}(\ln T)^{1/3}\big)$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected utilities against best fixed meta arm; argmax over discretized meta arms may be exponential in K, compute not stated. Remark D.6 gives Õ(K^{4/3}T^{2/3}) for single-arm activation (not recorded).

symbols.rho: ratio of estimation-stage rounds to phase length (algorithm parameter in (0,1))
symbols.gamma: time-discount factor of the impact function

conditions: impact function is time-discounted average (extends to |f_k(t+s)-g(p_k)|<=gamma^s)

source.label: theorem: key_theorem_neq_1
source.quote: For any constant ratio $\rho\in(0,1)$ and $\gamma\in(0,1)$, let $\epsilon= \Theta((\ln(T\rho)/(T\rho))^{1/3})$ and $s_a= \Theta(\ln(\epsilon^{1/3}/K)/\ln\gamma)$. The regret of Algorithm \ref{algo:reduction_algo} with Algorithm \ref{algo:history-dependent} as input bounds as follows: $\reg(T) = \cO\big( K T^{2/3}\left((\ln (T\rho))/\rho\right)^{1/3}\big)$.

conditions: hard instances: Bernoulli rewards with Lipschitz bump functions, L_k = 1

source.label: theorem_low_bound_all
source.quote: Let $T > 2K$ and $K \geq 4$, there exist problem instances that for our action- and history-dependent bandits, respectively, the regret for any algorithm $\cA$ follows: $\inf_{\cA} \reg(T) \geq \Omega(K T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: Action-dependent part; restated as Theorem F.2 in appendix. Proof shows observations of all base arms (via importance weighting).

conditions: reward functions satisfy the strictly proper utility property (Definition G.1)

source.label: theorem_low_bound_all
source.quote: Let $T > 2K$ and $K \geq 4$, there exist problem instances that for our action- and history-dependent bandits, respectively, the regret for any algorithm $\cA$ follows: $\inf_{\cA} \reg(T) \geq \Omega(K T^{2/3})$.

results.notes: History-dependent part via reduction to action-dependent case (Appendix G).

tuning: base algorithm with O(sqrt(|P_eps| T ln T)) regret on discretized meta arms

source.label: lemma:regret_bound_naive
source.quote: Let $\epsilon = \Theta \big(\big(\frac{\ln T}{T }\big)^\frac{1}{K+1}\big)$. Running a bandit algorithm which achieves optimal regret $\cO(\sqrt{|\cP_\epsilon|T\ln T})$ on the strategy space $\cP_\epsilon$ attains the following regret (w.r.t. the optimal arm in non-discretized $\cP$): $\reg(T) = \cO\big(T^{\frac{K}{K+1}}{(\ln T)}^{\frac{1}{K+1}}\big)$.

results.notes: Naive discretization baseline (e.g. UCB1 on discretized meta arms); constant hides K(L*)^{(K-1)/(K+1)}.
